method.name: milp_assignment_selection
steps: Define workers W = {I, II, III, IV, V} and tasks T = {A, B, C, D}
Binary variable x[w,t] = 1 if worker w is assigned to task t, else 0
Binary variable y[w] = 1 if worker w is selected (used in any task), else 0
Objective: minimize sum(w in W, t in T) time[w,t] * x[w,t]
Each task assigned to exactly one worker: for all t in T, sum(w in W) x[w,t] = 1
Each worker does at most one task: for all w in W, sum(t in T) x[w,t] <= 1
Link selection and assignment: x[w,t] <= y[w] for all w,t
Exactly 4 workers selected: sum(w in W) y[w] = 4
All x binary, y binary; solve with MILP solver

method.name: enumerate_assignment
steps: Identify all C(5,4) = 5 ways to choose 4 workers out of 5
For each selection of 4 workers, solve the resulting 4x4 assignment problem
For each worker subset, enumerate all 4! = 24 permutations of task assignments; compute total hours
Select the worker subset and permutation with minimum total hours
Return the global minimum across all 5 worker subsets

method.name: milp_assignment
steps: Define workers W = {I, II, III, IV, V} and tasks T = {A, B, C, D}
Binary variable x[w,t] = 1 if worker w is assigned to task t, else 0
Objective: minimize sum(w in W, t in T) time[w,t] * x[w,t]
Each task assigned to exactly one worker: for all t in T, sum(w in W) x[w,t] = 1
Each worker assigned to at most one task: for all w in W, sum(t in T) x[w,t] <= 1
Exactly 4 assignments: sum(w in W, t in T) x[w,t] = 4
All x binary; solve with MILP solver
